page.layout: Two medallion engravings with partial legends at the top, centred side by side; below them one column of running text. No marginal notes. Running head at top centre, page number at top left.

main_text.l: SICHE[?] VS.
DO[?]
SICHÆVS, Didonis auunculus[?] & vir, Herculis Sacerdos
fuit, qui honos secundus à rege erat. Hic opes non tectis, sed
terræ crediderat, quam rem etsi homines ignorabant, fama
tamen loquebatur: qua incensus Pygmalion, Didonis frater,
hunc sacrificiis intentum interfecit, cuius meminit his ver-si-
bus Vergilius.

l.i: Huic coniux Sichæus erat, ditissimus agri
Phœnicum: sed regna Tyri germanus habebat
Pygmalion, scelere ante alios immanior omnes,
Quos inter medius venit furor: ille Sichæum
Impius ante aras, atque auri cæcus amore,

main_text.l: Vide Iustin. lib. 18. & Vergil. lib. Ænei. 1. & 4.
DIDO Beli Phœnicum seu Tyriorum Regis filia, Pygma-
lionis soror, ac Sichæi uxor, occiso marito, astu usa in Africam
navigavit, cum thesauris quibus inhiaverat Pygmalion. Car-
thaginem condidit anno mundi 3076. ante Christum natum
886. ab ædificatione templi Salomonis 143. iuxta Iosephum
libro primo contra Apionem. huius castitas, cui notam inurere
tentavit Vergilius, eximiè laudatur à Boccacio, atque etiam ab
Ausonio: siquidem emori maluit quàm cum Hiarba Rege se-
cundis nuptiis coniungi. hæc proprio nomine Elisa dicta
est, Dido autem cognominata à rerum magnitudine, quasi virago.
Culta est ut Dea, templis, arisque eius nomini dicatis. Vide Iu-
stin.lib.18.Boc.lib.2.de casibus illustr.

page.notes: The two medallions are engraved portraits (Sichaeus left, Dido right). Their legends are only partly legible: left reads "SICHE" down the left edge and "VS." at top right; right shows "DO" with a star below. Read as partial; the missing letters are not printed in legible form. The word "auunculus" is doubtful: the printed u carries a mark above it. Some line-end hyphens are kept as printed. The catchword and signature are absent.
